item.title: Divergent Trajectories in the $3x+1$ Problem and a ${\em S}$- Units Equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.14569v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this note we assume the existence of divergent trajectories (if any) under the Collatz map and investigate the consequences of this assumption, even though the Conjecture of Collatz seems to be true. In a trajectory we show that the Diophantine exponential equation $x + y = w 2^n$ in the integers $x, y, w, n$ plays an important role. In this context the recent strong finiteness theorem of Bennett and Billerey on ${\it S}-Units has consequences on the set of prime numbers generated by a collection of local minima, called wave-minima (defined ad hoc for simplicity's sake) in a divergent trajectory. It allows to define canonically a density of a trajectory and some conjectures and open problems related to these prime numbers.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Louis Verger-Gaugry (USMB [Universit{\'e} de Savoie] [Universit{\'e} de Chamb{\'e}ry])

item.title: Random Chowla and Goldbach Conjectures
item.description: arXiv:2611.14579v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that for a Rademacher random multiplicative function $(f(n))_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ and any non-linear polynomial $P\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$ admitting a positive constant $\kappa_P$ such that \[\lim_{N\rightarrow\infty} \frac{\#\{n\in\left[N\right]:P(n)\text{ is square-free}\}}{N} =\kappa_P,\] we have \[ \frac{1}{\sqrt{\kappa_PN}}\sum_{n\leqslant N}f(P(n)) \xrightarrow[]{d}\mathcal{N}(0,1), \] as $N\rightarrow\infty $, where convergence is in distribution to a standard Gaussian. Using a direct combinatorial argument, we establish paucity estimates for non-trivial square products of square-free polynomial values at every fixed moment order. These estimates yield the Gaussian limit by the method of moments. We also study partial sums of the form $\sum_{n<N} F(f(n),f(N-n))$ for a suitable class of bivariate functions $F$ when $f$ is a Steinhaus random multiplicative function, and prove analogous results in special cases in the Rademacher setting. These results can be viewed as random analogues of the Goldbach-type problems considered by Mangerel.
item.dc:creator: Ihor Pylaiev

item.title: $\mathbb Z$ is Diophantine over $\mathbb Q$ with 28 unknowns
item.description: arXiv:2611.14605v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recently, OpenAI proved that Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the field $\mathbb Q$ of rational numbers has a negative solution. Motivated by this work, G. Conant et al. showed that $\mathbb Z$ is diophantine over $\mathbb Q$, i.e., there is an integer-coefficient polynomial $F(x,y_1,\ldots,y_n)$ such that for any $x\in\mathbb Q$ we have $$ x\in\mathbb Z\quad\iff \exists\,y_1,\ldots,y_{n}\in\mathbb Q\ [F(x,y_1,\ldots,y_{n})=0].$$ They constructed such a polynomial $F$ with deg $F=4$ and $n=393$. In this paper, we prove the existence of such a polynomial $F$ with $n=28$.
item.dc:creator: Zhi-Wei Sun

item.title: Encoding rational $\Delta$-triples on elliptic curves
item.description: arXiv:2611.14803v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A $\Delta$-triple for a natural number $n$ is a triple $(x,y,z)$ of divisors of $n$ with $1<x<y\leq z<\sqrt n$ and $n/x-x=(n/y-y)+(n/z-z)$. The numbers that admit such a triple are those with the $\Delta$ property, which governs the existence of certain $n$-simple triangles in factor graphs of split graphs. We allow the three components to be rational numbers, and show that, once the quotient $z/y=a/b$ is fixed, the rational $\Delta$-triples for $n$ are exactly the rational points of the elliptic curve $Y^2=n\,ab\,w(w+ab)\bigl(w+(a+b)^2\bigr)$ lying over the interval $-b(a+b)<w<-ab$. Since a rational $\Delta$-triple for $n$ amounts to $\Delta$-triples for infinitely many of the numbers $\kappa^2n$, the chord--tangent construction becomes a way of producing new $\Delta$-triples from old ones. For perfect squares, the curve always carries a rational point coming from a degenerate triple. This point has order $4$ if $a=b$, and infinite order if $a>b$. As a consequence, for every quotient $a/b>1$ there are infinitely many pairwise non-proportional $\Delta$-triples of perfect squares with $z/y=a/b$, in contrast with the fact that perfect squares have no $\Delta$-triple with $y=z$. For arbitrary $n$, there are infinitely many rational $\Delta$-triples for $n$ with a given quotient if and only if the corresponding curve has positive rank.
item.dc:creator: Victor N. Schv\"ollner

item.title: Equilateral simplices over general fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.14845v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A classical theorem of Schoenberg (1937) characterizes the dimensions $d$ for which $\mathbb{Q}^d$ contains the vertex set of a regular simplex with $d+1$ vertices. We generalize Schoenberg's result to all fields of characteristic not equal to $2$, using elementary Witt theory and Lagrange's four-square theorem. Our generalization also sharpens Schoenberg's theorem and complements more recent work of Lorenz and Zimmermann (2026) by characterizing the admissible edge lengths. In the case of finite characteristic, equilateral simplices with $d+2$ vertices can sometimes exist (F.~Rad\'o 1986), and we characterize this situation as well, again for all fields of characteristic not equal to $2$. We also briefly consider the edge lengths of equilateral simplices of $d$ vertices.
item.dc:creator: Konrad J. Swanepoel

item.title: Random Diophantine inequalities in few variables
item.description: arXiv:2611.14865v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that for almost all additive Diophantine inequalities of degree $k$ in at least $k+1$ variables the expected asymptotic formula for the density of solutions holds true. This improves the result of Br\"udern and Dietmann \cite{BD}.
item.dc:creator: Yu-Chen Sun, Xuanzhe Wang, Lilu Zhao

item.title: Rational isogenies of of rank-two Drinfeld modules
item.description: arXiv:2611.14873v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the $\mathbb{F}_{q}(T)$-rational points on the Drinfeld modular curves $X_{0}(\mathfrak{n})$ of arbitrary level, obtaining a complete classification of rational cyclic isogenies of rank-two Drinfeld $\mathbb{F}_{q}[T]$-modules over $\mathbb{F}_{q}(T)$. As consequences, we prove Schweizer's conjecture on rational torsion, establish optimal uniform bounds on the number of isomorphism classes in an $\mathbb{F}_{q}(T)$-isogeny class of rank-two Drinfeld $\mathbb{F}_{q}[T]$-modules and determine the geometric automorphism groups of $X_{0}(\mathfrak{p})$ for primes $\mathfrak{p}$ of degree at least three.
item.dc:creator: Shun Ishii, Ryotaro Sakamoto

item.title: On the moduli of distinct covering systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.15110v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 2022, Balister, Bollob\'as, Morris, Sahasrabudhe, and Tiba proved that the least common multiple of the moduli in any distinct covering system with odd moduli is divisible by $9$ or $15$. We strengthen this necessary condition to divisibility by $45$ and prove that the minimum modulus of an odd distinct covering system is at most $9$. For arbitrary distinct moduli, we lower the upper bound of Balister et al.\ on the minimum modulus from $616000$ to $14000$. For distinct squarefree moduli, we lower the upper bound of $118$ obtained by Cummings, Filaseta, and Trifonov in 2025 to $7$. Our proofs combine the distortion method with a joint comparison based on directional convexity. The comparison uses independent random exponents to bound expectations of convex functions of sums of indicators of residue classes, while retaining the restrictions on the allowed moduli. A sharper bound for the conditional density on each fibre further improves the estimates for the subsequent stages of the distortion process.
item.dc:creator: Xiangjun Dai, Huixi Li, Junfeng Li, Shaoyun Yi

item.title: Computing extensions of flag-jump t-modules
item.description: arXiv:2611.15116v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Anderson t-modules whose positive-degree coefficient matrices admit a flag-jump basis and extend the t-reduction algorithm to this setting. We prove that these t-modules are abelian, with motive rank equal to the sum of their jump degrees. If $\Phi$ has jump degrees $j_1,\ldots,j_d$ and $deg_\tau\Psi<\min_s j_s$, we compute the t-module structure on ${\mathbf{Ext}}^1_\tau(\Phi,\Psi)$, its subgroup ${\mathbf{Ext}}_{0,\tau}(\Phi,\Psi)$, and the associated exact sequence. The construction allows nonzero nilpotent constant terms and includes the strictly pure case. When $\Psi$ is the Carlitz module, $N_\Phi=0$, and all jump degrees are at least two, the construction yields a dual t-module. We give complexity bounds for the algorithms and implementations in SymPy and Mathematica.
item.dc:creator: D. E. K\k{e}dzierski, D. Koellmer, P. Kraso\'n

item.title: Congruence properties modulo powers of 3 for designated summands in partitions into odd parts
item.description: arXiv:2611.15164v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\textup{PDO}_\textup{t}(n)$ denote the total number of tagged parts over all partitions of $n$ into odd parts with designated summands. Using $3$-dissection identities and coefficient extraction, we obtain explicit polynomial expansions for the generating functions of two infinite families of arithmetic subsequences of $\textup{PDO}_\textup{t}(n)$. We establish lower bounds for the $3$-adic valuations of the coefficients in these expansions, thereby proving two infinite families of congruences modulo powers of 3 conjectured by Lin (J. Number Theory,~2018). We then estimate the $3$-adic valuations of two-by-two determinants formed from consecutive coefficient vectors. These estimates yield two infinite families of internal congruences modulo high powers of $3$.
item.dc:creator: Xingyi Li, Dazhao Tang

item.title: On least periods of a class of arithmetic functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.15379v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $k, a, c$ be positive integers, let $b$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $f$ be a nonvanishing complex-valued multiplicative function. Qian, Tan and Hong proved that $$G_f(n)=\frac{\prod\limits_{i=0}^k f(b+a(n+i c))}{f\left(\operatorname*{lcm}\limits_{0 \leq i \leq k}\{b+a(n+i c)\}\right)}$$ is periodic and asked for its least positive period. In this paper, we answer this problem by giving an explicit formula for this period in terms of finitely many values of $f$ at prime powers. In particular, we determine the least periods for $f(n)=\sigma_\alpha(n)=\sum\limits_{d \mid n} d^\alpha$ for every real $\alpha$, and for $f(n)=n^{\varepsilon}$ for every real $\varepsilon$.
item.dc:creator: Wen-Jie Huang, Quan-Hui Yang

item.title: Integers with many divisors in a dyadic interval
item.description: arXiv:2611.15534v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We find the correct order of magnitude for the number of $n\leq x$ having at least $r$ divisors in the interval $(y,2y]$, uniformly in a wide range of the parameters $x,y,r$.
item.dc:creator: Kevin Ford, Mikhail R. Gabdullin, Kyle Pratt

item.title: Prime values of linear forms and a quadratic form: one proof and two arithmetic applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.16062v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $L_1,\dots,L_k\in \mathbb Z[x,y]$ be a system of linear polynomials whose homogeneous parts are pairwise linearly independent. Let $K=\mathbb Q(\alpha)$ be an imaginary quadratic field. Utilizing the higher order Fourier analysis machinery of Green and Sawhney in their breakthrough work on the Gaussian prime conjecture, we show that if there are no local obstructions, then there are infinitely many $(x,y)\in \mathbb Z$ such that $L_1(x,y),\dots,L_k(x,y),$ and $N_{K/\mathbb Q}(x+y\alpha)$ are simultaneously prime. We further establish an asymptotic formula which matches the prediction by the multivariate Bateman-Horn conjecture. We present two arithmetic applications of this prime counting result. First, we show that the Brauer--Manin obstruction is the only obstruction to weak approximation on a new family of varieties, including diagonal conic bundles all of whose degenerate fibres are defined over $\mathbb Q$ except one fibre that may be defined over an imaginary quadratic field. Second, we construct elliptic curves over $\mathbb Q$ with infinitely many quadratic twists of rank exactly two.
item.dc:creator: Niven Achenjang, Katharine Woo

item.title: A Diophantine definition of $\mathbb{Z}$ in $\mathbb{Q}$
item.description: arXiv:2611.16130v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the integers form a Diophantine subset of the rational numbers. More precisely, there exist an integer $n\ge1$ and a polynomial $P\in\mathbb{Z}[T,W_1,\dots,W_n]$ of total degree at most four such that $q\in\mathbb{Q}$ is an integer if and only if $P(q,\mathbf w)=0$ for some $\mathbf w\in\mathbb{Q}^n$. Consequently, any recursively enumerable subset of $\mathbb{Q}^r$ is Diophantine, and Mazur's conjecture on the topology of rational points fails. The proof is inspired by OpenAI's work on Hilbert's tenth problem over $\mathbb{Q}$. It does not use the $2$-converse or the $2$-adic Fontaine--Mazur results announced and employed by OpenAI. We define the rational numbers with square denominator using rational points on certain quadratic twists of the congruent number elliptic curve. The criterion of Tian, Yuan and Zhang, in Smith's formulation, implies that these quadratic twists have analytic rank one. A height estimate for rational points on a fixed quotient of a Shimura curve allows us to express multiplication of elliptic-curve indices. We obtain this estimate by bounding the modular levels of the associated quaternionic abelian surfaces. The level bound is based on a compatible system of Galois representations over $\mathbb{Q}$ with controlled ramification and on Khare--Wintenberger's proof of Serre's conjecture. Green--Tao--Ziegler's theorem on linear patterns of primes supplies the rational solutions needed for a Diophantine model of integer arithmetic.
item.dc:creator: Ashay Burungale

item.title: Congruences Modulo 16, 32 and 64 for a Restricted Overpartition Function
item.description: arXiv:2611.16145v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\overline{t}^{(3)}(n)$ denote the number of overpartitions of $n$ in which consecutive parts differ by a multiple of $3$ unless the larger part is overlined, and the smallest part is overlined unless it is divisible by $3$. Using dissections of theta functions, we establish two infinite families of congruences modulo $32$ and $64$. We also obtain two residue formulas modulo $16$ and use them to derive four further infinite families of congruences modulo $16$. In particular, for every positive integer $M$ and nonnegative integer $n$, the residue of $\overline{t}^{(3)}(M^2(18n+12))$ modulo $16$ is $8$ if $6n+4$ is a square and $0$ otherwise.
item.dc:creator: Li Zhang, Qiao-Mei Zhang

item.title: Many more odd zeta values are irrational
item.description: arXiv:2611.16156v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that for any sufficiently large odd integer $s$, there exist at least \[ 2.78 \, \sqrt{\frac{s \log\log s}{\log s}} \] irrational values among $\zeta(3), \zeta(5), \dots, \zeta(s)$, where $\zeta$ is the Riemann zeta function. This improves on the best known estimate by a constant factor times $\sqrt{ \log\log s}$. The proof combines the elimination technique and an arithmetic lemma of Fischler--Sprang--Zudilin, the hypergeometric constructions of Lai--Yu, and the Hankel determinant method that appeared in the proof that $\zeta(5)$ is irrational posted by Fauzan on September 17, 2026.
item.dc:creator: St\'ephane Fischler, Li Lai, Johannes Sprang, Wadim Zudilin

item.title: Admissibility of unbounded complexes of smooth representations
item.description: arXiv:2611.16167v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a $p$-adic Lie group and $k$ a field of characteristic $p$. We prove that a complex of smooth $k$-representations of $G$ has admissible cohomology if and only if it is globally admissible, i.e., its hypercohomology with respect to a torsion-free open compact pro-$p$ subgroup is finite dimensional in every degree. This extends the bounded-below and bounded-above comparison of Schneider--Sorensen to arbitrary unbounded complexes.
item.dc:creator: Hargun Bhatia

item.title: Stationary Phase along Rays and the Determinant of Linearly Constrained Kloosterman Families
item.description: arXiv:2611.16254v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the top-weight sheaf $\mathcal W_n$ of linearly constrained Kloosterman sums over finite fields of odd characteristic, of rank $r(n)=2^n-\binom n{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$. A local Fourier-transform analysis describes wild monodromy at infinity along rays through nonescaping critical points and their quadratic characters, giving explicit Swan conductors and the escape locus. The resulting stationary-phase description yields a ray-theoretic proof of the geometric determinant. A reflection pairing and a Frobenius calculation at the tame endpoint recover the arithmetic determinant $\det\mathcal W_n\simeq\mathcal L_\psi(-2^{n-1}\lambda^{-1}\sum_i h_i)\otimes\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell(-(n+1)r(n)/2)$. We obtain reciprocity for exterior-power Frobenius traces, the exact distribution of normalized determinants, and spectral compression on symmetric loci. Assuming the ambient connected-monodromy theorem from companion work, we determine the monodromy of the geometric generic ray. Further results include bounds for complete exponential sums, conductor identities for selected parameter curves, and the Euler characteristic of the parameter torus. Rank-two boundary conormal calculations are separated from higher-codimension characteristic-cycle recursions, which remain conditional on explicit microlocal hypotheses.
item.dc:creator: Hamed Ebadi

item.title: Integral Exponential Series: Fibonacci Weights and Implicit Equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.16283v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We apply classical prime-power congruence criteria to two families of exponential series. For the Fibonacci numbers $F_n$, we characterize the polynomials \(P\in\Z[T]\) for which $\exp(\sum_{n\ge1}P(F_n)x^n/n)$ has integer coefficients: this holds if and only if $P$ is even and $P(0)\equiv P(1)\equiv P(2)\pmod5$. In particular, $5$ is the least positive multiplier for each positive even power of $F_n$, and the series with weights $5F_n^{2k}$ has degree $5^{k-1}$ over \(\Q(x)\) for $k\ge1$. For \(R_n(y)\in\Z[y]\) satisfying $R_{pn}(y)\equiv R_n(y)\pmod p$ for every prime $p$ and every $n\ge1$, we prove that $H(x,y)=\exp(\sum_{n\ge1}R_n(y)^n x^n/n)$ belongs to \(\Z[y][[x]]\) and that $A(x)=H(x,A(x))$ has a unique integral solution. For \(q\in \Z\), taking $R_n(y)=q^n+y$ proves the conjecture in OEIS A163138; the Fibonacci result proves the conjecture in A207969 and A207970. For the implicit family with indeterminate $q$, the coefficient of $x^n$ has degree $n^2$, leading coefficient $1/n$, and nonnegative integer coefficients in the binomial basis, for every $n\ge1$.
item.dc:creator: J. P. Li, Y. M. Zhong, Y. B. Zhou

item.title: Postcritically Finite Unicritical Polynomials over CM Fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.16354v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A rational map of degree at least two is postcritically finite (PCF) if every critical point has a finite forward orbit. For the unicritical family $f_{d,c}(z)=z^d+c$ with $d\ge2$, we call $c$ a PCF parameter if $f_{d,c}$ is PCF. As discussed by Baker and DeMarco, these parameters are analogous to $j$-invariants of elliptic curves with complex multiplication. For every $d\ge2$, we determine which PCF parameters lie in a CM field. The same list gives all PCF parameters over the maximal abelian extension of $\mathbb{Q}$. This extends the classifications of Noytaptim and Petsche over the maximal totally real extension of $\mathbb{Q}$ and of Ferraguti and Pagano over quadratic number fields. The proof uses the totally real classification in degree two, orbit bounds, Kronecker's theorem, Goksel's unit theorem, Lam--Leung's short-sum classification, cyclotomic averages, and known irreducibility results.
item.dc:creator: Kaoru Sano

item.title: Optimal Sample Complexity for Genus-Two Zeta Functions from Noisy Random Euler Products
item.description: arXiv:2611.16358v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study exact recovery of the Hasse--Weil zeta numerator from repeated noisy observations of a randomized Euler product. For a genus-two curve over $\mathbb{F}_q$, we attach independent symmetric signs to its closed points and observe the logarithm of the resulting product at $t_q=c/\sqrt q$, where $0<c<1/\sqrt{12}$ is fixed. For every fixed, known additive noise density $f$ satisfying $\sqrt{f}\in H^1(\mathbb{R})$, we prove that the minimax number of independent observations required for exact recovery with error probability at most $\delta$ has order $q^4\log(1/\delta)$. No moment condition is imposed on the noise, so the result includes Cauchy readout. The upper bound estimates the phase of an empirical characteristic function and uses the separation of the integral Weil coefficients. The matching lower bound compares the full observation laws for two actual curves with ordinary, absolutely simple Jacobians. It combines a binomial comparison with a uniform bound on the closed-point tail. Thus access to the full observations does not improve the sample order attained by the phase estimator. The result concerns the information in a specified observation channel. It does not assume an efficient implementation of that channel.
item.dc:creator: Taro Hayashi, Ryoichi Suzuki

item.title: p-adic Height Pairing through Higher Class Field Theory: Part I
item.description: arXiv:2611.16379v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a p-adic height pairing for curves with split degenerate stable reduction over the prime p using the higher class field theory of Kato-Saito. We then show this pairing coincide with the standard Coleman-Gross p-adic height pairing when extended to the semistable reduction case using methods by Besser and Vologodsky.
item.dc:creator: Yuhui Yao

item.title: The solutions of the Diophantine equation $(2^{k}-1)(3^{l}-1)=7^{m}-1$
item.description: arXiv:2611.16437v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we will show that the positive integer triple $(k,l,m)$ satisfying the equation in the title is $(2,1,1).$
item.dc:creator: Zafer \c{S}iar, Refik Keskin

item.title: A sharp bound for the $a$-number of a cyclic cover of $\mathbb{P}^1$
item.description: arXiv:2611.16449v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth projective curve of genus $g$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>2$. We give upper bounds for the $a$-number $a(X)$ when $X$ is hyperelliptic or, more generally, a tame cyclic cover of the projective line. For hyperelliptic curves, writing $g=pm+r$ with $0\le r<p$ and $n=(p-1)/2$, we prove the sharp bound $a(X)\le nm+\min\{n,r\}$. For tame cyclic covers, we refine previously known upper bounds and give curves attaining the resulting bound in infinitely many genera in characteristics $3$ and $5$. The proofs combine an alternating pairing on the bundle of locally exact differentials, originally due to Raynaud, with an explicit polynomial description of the Cartier operator. We also produce an explicit locus of hyperelliptic curves $X$ with $a(X)\ge a_g$, where $\frac{a_g}{g}$ converges to $\frac{p-1}{2p}$ as $g$ goes to $\infty$, whose dimension grows linearly with the genus $g$. These families exhibit excess intersections of the Torelli locus with loci of large $a$-number in the moduli space of principally polarized abelian varieties.
item.dc:creator: Shiva Chidambaram

item.title: The Evertse-Ferretti interval result for a set of weights, and the exponent $1/2$ in three complexity bounds
item.description: arXiv:2611.16536v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The interval result of Evertse and Ferretti (2013) concerns a tuple $L$ of linear forms and one tuple $c$ of weights. It says that the parameters $Q$ for which the twisted height $H_{L,c,Q}$ has a small value outside an exceptional subspace $T(L,c)$ lie in $O(\delta^{-2}\log\delta^{-1})$ intervals $[Q_i,Q_i^{\omega})$. We prove this for a whole set $\mathcal{C}$ of weights with the same forms. At most $J$ subspaces $T(L,c)$ occur, where $J$ depends only on the dimension and on the number of places, and one family of $O(\delta^{-2}\log\delta^{-1})$ intervals serves every $c\in\mathcal{C}$ at once. Neither count depends on $\mathcal{C}$. In applications of Bugeaud-Evertse type the solutions are sorted into about $\varepsilon^{-1}$ classes with the same forms and different weights, and one application now serves all classes. We deduce three complexity bounds. For a real algebraic irrational number $\xi$, the number $p(n,\xi,b)$ of blocks of length $n$ in its base-$b$ expansion satisfies $\limsup p(n,\xi,b)/(n(\log n)^\eta)=\infty$ for every $\eta<1/2$; Bugeaud and Evertse proved this for $\eta<1/11$. The same holds for the continued fraction expansion of an algebraic number of degree at least three, and for the steering word of $(3/2)^n$. We explain why $1/2$ is the limit of the method. All results are machine-verified in Lean~4.
item.dc:creator: Ralf Stephan

item.title: Central limit theorems for Frobenius, Hecke and Kloosterman angles
item.description: arXiv:2611.16550v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Frobenius angles of non-CM elliptic curves and the Hecke angles of non-CM newforms are equidistributed with respect to the Sato--Tate measure, while for Kloosterman angles, this is known on average over natural families. We study the fluctuations around these laws in large families, for smooth test functions. We prove an unconditional central limit theorem for Frobenius angles of elliptic curves for a much larger class of test functions than previously considered; earlier results assumed the Riemann hypothesis for $L$-functions of Hecke eigenforms of full level. This result follows from a general framework, developed here, which yields Gaussian moments for statistics of sequences in $[0,1]$ varying over families. In this framework, independence is replaced by two quantitative conditions: approximate independence at distinct indices, and convergence of the family averages to the Weyl limits at a suitable rate. As further applications, we extend central limit theorems for Kloosterman angles and for Hecke angles of newforms to larger classes of test functions, the latter with the weight and the level varying simultaneously. We also treat the dilated angles $\alpha\theta$ for integers $\alpha\geq2$, whose limiting distribution is uniform. Finally, we discuss sharp statistics, obtaining a central limit theorem for Hecke angles and explaining the obstruction for the other two families.
item.dc:creator: Shreyas Pai, Kaneenika Sinha, Naman Thakkar

item.title: Proof of the Quasi Riemann Hypothesis using $\mathbb Q[i]$
item.description: arXiv:2611.16665v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using quartic Gauss sums in place of the cubic Gauss sums in OpenAI's original proof, we prove that the Dedekind $\zeta$-function $\zeta_{\mathbb Q(i)}(s)$ of $\mathbb Q(i)$ has no zeros in the half-plane $\Re s>599/600$, thereby obtaining the same zero-free half-plane for the Riemann $\zeta$-function.We obtain the upper bound for the smoothed sum by applying Poisson summation twice and using the functional equation of the quartic Kubota series of angular weight $1$.In the Mellin representation, a zero-density bound for the family of quartic characters controls the terms from nonprincipal characters,and a residue and a lattice average over fourth powers give the main term.
item.dc:creator: Xin Hang Ji

item.title: Higher moments of twisted Kloosterman sums and the arithmetic of algebraic varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.16713v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For an odd prime $p,$ consider the affine varieties $X_k: \sum\limits_{i=1}^{k}(x_i+x_i^{-1})=0$ over the finite field $\F_p.$ In this paper, a key feature of our work is arithmetic interpretation between the higher power moments of Kloosterman sums, modular forms and arithmetic geometry of the varieties $X_5$ and $X_6$ through their rational point counts. Our main results provide two distinct explicit formulas for the point count $\#X_5(\F_p).$ In the first formula, we express $\#X_5(\F_p)$ in terms of Fourier coefficients of modular forms and a certain weighted average of fourth power twisted Kloosterman moments, where the average is taken over multiplicative characters. We further establish an identity expressing this weighted average of fourth power moment of twisted Kloosterman sums in terms of fifth power quadratic twisted Kloosterman moment, together with Fourier coefficients of modular forms. Moreover, we derive an independent expression for the same average with different weight directly in terms of Fourier coefficients of modular forms. In the second identity for $\#X_5(\F_p)$, we express this purely in terms of Fourier coefficients of two modular forms. Moreover, we express $\#X_6(\F_p),$ in terms of Fourier coefficients of three modular forms. For these two expressions of $\#X_5(\F_p)$ and $\#X_6(\F_p),$ our approach is based on an identity that relates the point counts of $X_k$ to the $k$-th power moments of Kloosterman sum and its quadratic twist.
item.dc:creator: Manash Dutta, Neelam Saikia

item.title: Finiteness of strongly reflective modular forms
item.description: arXiv:2611.16819v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\Gamma\subset\mathrm{O}^+(n,2)$ be a rational arithmetic group with $n\geq 3$. A non-constant modular form for $\Gamma$ is called strongly reflective if its zero divisor is a reduced union of mirrors of reflections in $\Gamma$. We show that, up to conjugation and multiplication by a nonzero scalar, there are only finitely many strongly reflective modular forms. As a consequence, we establish the finiteness of holomorphic automorphic products of singular weight. These results answer a question posed by Borcherds in 1995 and settle a conjecture of Gritsenko--Nikulin from 1998. As an application, up to conjugation, we prove the finiteness of $\Gamma$ whose corresponding algebra of modular forms is freely generated. The key ingredient is a uniform upper bound on the covolume of $\Gamma$, obtained by adapting the higher-rank lattice convergence theorem of Ab\'ert et al. to the study of the degrees of reflective branch divisors.
item.dc:creator: Jialin Li, Haowu Wang

item.title: Estimates of short exponential sums with primes in major arcs
item.description: arXiv:2611.16828v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When solving a number of additive problems with almost equal summands, along with estimating short trigonometric sums with primes of the form $$ S_k(\alpha;x,y)=\sum_{x-y<n\le x}\Lambda(n)e(\alpha n^k), $$ on the minor arcs, estimates of these sums on the major arcs are also needed, except in a small neighborhood of their centers, as well as an asymptotic formula in a small neighborhood of the center of the major arcs. In this paper, using the second moment of Dirichlet $L$-functions on the critical line, for $S_k(\alpha;x,y)$ on the major arcs $\mathfrak{M}(\mathscr{L}^b)$, $\tau=y^5x^{-2}\mathscr{L}^{-b_1}$, $\mathscr{L} =\ln xq$, except in a small neighborhood of their centers $|\alpha-\frac{a}{q}|>\left(2\pi k^2x^{k-2}y^2\right)^{-1}$, for $y\ge x^{1-\frac{1}{2k-1+\eta_k}}\mathscr{L}^{c_k}$, $$ \eta_k=\frac{2}{4k-5+2\sqrt{(2k-2)(2k-3)}}, \qquad c_k= \frac{2A+22+\left(\frac{2\sqrt{2k-3}}{\sqrt{2k-2}}-1\right)b_1}{2\sqrt{(2k-2)(2k-3)}-(2k-3)}, $$ a nontrivial estimate of the form $$ S_k(\alpha;x,y)\ll y\mathscr{L}^{-A}, $$ is obtained, where $A$, $b_1$, $b$ are arbitrary fixed positive numbers, and an asymptotic formula is proved in a small neighborhood of the centers of the major arcs.
item.dc:creator: Zarullo Rakhmonov

item.title: Congruences involving the products of three binomial coefficients II
item.dc:creator: Zhi-Hong Sun

item.title: Differential properties of Drinfeld modular forms
item.description: arXiv:2611.16909v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the action of vector fields on the Drinfeld symmetric spaces on de Rham classes of the generic Drinfeld module. The resulting Kodaira-Spencer map is an isomorphism, and is described by the Jacobian matrix \(J := (\frac{\partial g_{j}}{\partial \omega_{i}})_{1 \leq i,j \leq r}\), where the \(g_{j}\) are the basic coefficient modular forms of rank \(r\). We show that \(J\) is the matrix inverse of the period matrix \(P\) that results from the de Rham theory of Drinfeld modules. We define the notion of Drinfeld modular differential form, which generalizes the transformation behavior of Drinfeld modular forms from functions to differential \(n\)-forms on the Drinfeld symmetric space \(\Omega^{r}\). The algebra \(\mathbf{M}^{(*)} = \bigoplus_{0 \leq n < r} \mathbf{M}^{(n)}\) of all such is provided with a Serre derivation \(D \colon \mathbf{M}^{(n)} \to \mathbf{M}^{(n+1)}\) from \(n\)-forms to \((n+1)\)-forms, where \(\mathbf{M}^{(0)} = \mathbf{M}\) is the algebra of customary modular forms for \(\mathrm{GL}(r, \mathbb{F}_{q}[T])\). We determine the structure of \(\mathbf{M}^{(*)}\), which turns out to be the exterior algebra \(\bigwedge (\mathbf{M}^{(1)})\) of the \(\mathbf{M}\)-module \(\mathbf{M}^{(1)}\).
item.dc:creator: Ernst-Ulrich Gekeler

item.title: Finite multiple harmonic sums and lower-truncated $p$-adic multiple zeta-star values
item.description: arXiv:2611.16923v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce lower-truncated $p$-adic multiple zeta-star values and construct their harmonic regularizations. We show that they are independent of the branch of the $p$-adic logarithm and satisfy harmonic product relations. We express finite multiple harmonic sums as alternating convolutions of harmonic-regularized $p$-adic multiple zeta values and lower-truncated $p$-adic multiple zeta-star values. This gives a $p$-adic analogue of the classical truncation identity, which reduces to the inversion relation between ordinary and star harmonic-regularized values when the truncation point is $1$. For truncation point $p$, it relates finite multiple zeta values to $p$-adic multiple zeta values.
item.dc:creator: Ku-Yu Fan, Hidekazu Furusho

item.title: Permutation polynomials of given index up to quasi-multiplicative equivalence
item.description: arXiv:2611.16944v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $q$ be a prime power and let $\ell$ be a divisor of $q-1$. We classify the permutation polynomials of $\mathbb F_q$ of polynomial index exactly $\ell$ up to quasi-multiplicative equivalence $G(X)\equiv uF(vX^d)\pmod{X^q-X}$, where $u,v\in\mathbb F_q^*$ and $\gcd(d,q-1)=1$, and we count the classes. For polynomials vanishing at $0$, the classes are the orbits of an explicit finite group on vectors of values at the $\ell$-th roots of unity. Through the permutation it induces on the roots of unity, each orbit lies over a double coset of the symmetric group $S_\ell$ with respect to its translation subgroup and an explicit affine group, and the stabilizers are explicit. For polynomials with nonzero constant term the action is free. Burnside's lemma, M\"obius inversion over the coefficient support and congruences along the cycles of affine permutations give an exact formula for the number of classes. For fixed $\ell\geqslant2$ these numbers are quasi-polynomials in $s=(q-1)/\ell$ of degree at most $\ell-1$, with period dividing $\ell$ for odd $\ell$ and $2\ell$ for even $\ell$; for polynomials vanishing at $0$ the degree is exactly $\ell-1$, and we determine the leading coefficient. For odd prime $\ell$ and for $\ell=4$ the counts are given in closed form. For index four we also count the binomials and trinomials at each admissible coefficient support. The sums of two binomial counts that occur are expressed through quartic Jacobi sums and Frobenius traces of elliptic curves and of a curve of genus two; one of the elliptic curves is the reduction of the curve $Y^2=X^3+8X^2+32X$, which has no complex multiplication over $\mathbb Q$. The trinomial counts are expressed through quartic cyclotomic numbers and these sums. All these terms cancel when the counts with a fixed residue of the vanishing order modulo $s$ are added.
item.dc:creator: Xiang Fan

item.title: Why should $\mathbb{Z}$ be Diophantine in $\mathbb{Q}$?
item.description: arXiv:2611.17124v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a Diophantine definition of the integers in the rational numbers conditional on the $abc$ conjecture, Dickson's conjecture, and finiteness of $2$-primary parts of Shafarevich--Tate groups. We also discuss some consequences of the existence of a Diophantine definition of the integers in the rational numbers. The goal of this work is to serve as an entry point to recent developments around Hilbert's tenth problem for the rational numbers.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Kozachinskiy, Hector Pasten, Xavier Vidaux

item.title: On the multidimensional polynomial Szemer\'{e}di theorem
item.description: arXiv:2611.17136v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the multidimensional polynomial Szemer\'{e}di theorem over prime fields. Let $P_1,\dots,P_m\in\F_p[t]^k$ be block independent vector polynomials of degree at most $d$, with $P_i(0)=0$ for every $i$. We prove that there is a constant $c=c(k,m,d)>0$ such that, for every sufficiently large prime $p$, every set $A\subset\F_p^k$ with $|A|\ge p^{k-c}$ contains a configuration $x,x+P_1(t),\dots,x+P_m(t)$ with $t\in\F_p\setminus\{0\}$.
item.dc:creator: Danqing He, Xuancheng Shao

item.title: Irregular weight-one Eisenstein series and Euler systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.17210v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $f=E_1(\chi_1,\chi_2)$ be an irregular Eisenstein series of weight one, that is, with $\chi_1(p)=\chi_2(p)$, and consider the generically cuspidal ordinary family passing through it. When $\chi_1$, $\chi_2$ and $\chi_1\chi_2^{-1}$ are primitive of the same conductor, we show that the specialization at $f$ of the modular-symbol $p$-adic $L$-function of this family, with periods taken in the cohomology of the compactified modular curves, factors as a product of two Kubota--Leopoldt $p$-adic $L$-functions attached to $\chi_1$ and $\chi_2$. Since there are no complex critical values in weight one, the factorization is obtained directly from the cohomological construction: we compute the tame-twisted modular measure by means of the localized Sharifi map and explicit reciprocity, and show that tame twisting identifies the compact period modules at weight one. This gives a weight-one analogue of the factorization of Bella\"iche--Dasgupta for critical-slope Eisenstein series. As applications, and under explicit specialization hypotheses, we compare Kato classes with circular units, Heegner classes with elliptic units, and diagonal cycles with Kato classes through two successive Eisenstein degenerations. We also discuss the passage from compact to open periods, and include an exposition of the congruence and degeneration methods underlying these comparisons.
item.dc:creator: Javier Polo, \'Oscar Rivero

item.title: The lifting problem for Galois representations of global fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.17255v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that all mod $2$ Galois representations of a global field lift modulo $4$. In contrast, for every odd prime $p$, we exhibit examples of global Galois representations modulo $p$ that do not lift modulo $p^2$. Our methods also allow us to prove liftability of generalized quaternion groups and hence to complete the classification of liftable finite groups initiated by Khare and Merkurjev.
item.dc:creator: Federico Scavia

item.title: Additive Relations and Betti Growth in Goldbach Rings
item.description: arXiv:2611.14580v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The binary Goldbach ring over a field $k$ is the quotient of $R=k[x_p:p\text{ an odd prime}]$ by the relations $x_px_q=x_{p'}x_{q'}$ whenever $p+q=p'+q'$, with $\deg x_p=(p,1)$. We prove that if $g$ is a map from the odd primes to an abelian group and $g(p)+g(q)$ depends only on $p+q$, then $g(p)=g(3)+\frac{p-3}{2}(g(5)-g(3))$ for every odd prime $p$. This settles K\'atai and Phong's conjecture on shifted prime arguments and proves, for odd primes, the affine classification they conjectured for binary sums. The universal group of binary prime relations is free of rank two. We obtain a minimal bigraded free resolution from compatible resolutions of finite truncations and determine the growth of its linear Betti numbers in two regimes. For fixed monomial degree $d\ge3$, as the Goldbach degree $n\to\infty$ through $n\equiv d\pmod2$, we prove $\beta_{d-1,n,d}\sim(d-1)T_d(n)/d!$, where $T_d(n)$ counts ordered representations by $d$ odd primes. Explicit Koszul cycles from common prime shifts span a positive fraction of this strand. For finite supports $\mathcal{A}_m=\{p\le m:p\text{ an odd prime}\}$, fix the homological degree $i\ge1$ and sum over all Goldbach degrees. As $m\to\infty$, the linear-strand totals are asymptotic to $i|\mathcal{A}_m|^{i+1}/(i+1)!$ when all binary relations on $\mathcal{A}_m$ are retained, and to $(1-2^{-i})|\mathcal{A}_m|^{i+1}/(i+1)!$ when only relations of common weight at most $m$ are retained. These leading estimates are uniform over fields. The interpolation theorem gives eventual depth at most two for the variable truncations; both truncation families have asymptotically maximal projective dimension.
item.dc:creator: Michael Nelson

item.title: Incidence Geometry of Local Maxima: Howe Duality and Branching
item.description: arXiv:2611.14591v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a finite-dimensional unitary representation of a finite or compact group, consider the mean squared matrix coefficient on the unit sphere. Its local maxima are the vectors generating irreducible cyclic subrepresentations. We show that for compatible group actions this variational picture retains the incidence structure of representation theory. For two commuting actions, intersections of projectivized local-maximal components recover the weighted support graph of the product representation, including its multiplicity spaces; Howe duality is the multiplicity-one matching case. More generally, for pairwise commuting actions, and for subgroup chains, every positive linear combination of the corresponding functionals has exactly their common local maxima, while every other critical point has a positive Hessian direction. On a fixed irreducible module at the top of a subgroup chain, the simultaneous projective local-maximal components are indexed by vertex paths in the weighted Bratteli diagram. Each component is the product of the projective space of the bottom representation and the projectivized branching multiplicity spaces. In the multiplicity-free case with one-dimensional bottom type, these reduce to the Gelfand-Tsetlin lines. Peter-Weyl, Frobenius reciprocity, Young branching and Schur-Weyl duality provide concrete instances of the general picture.
item.dc:creator: Pin-Chi Hung, Ming-Hsuan Kang

item.title: Cyclic fibers and exponential lower bounds for Erd\H{o}s--Ginzburg--Ziv constants
item.description: arXiv:2611.15210v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that for every integer $n\ge2$ that is not a power of two there are constants $c_n>0$ and $B_n>2$ such that $s(C_n^r)\ge c_nB_n^r$ for all $r\ge1$. For powers of two, Harborth's formula gives growth rate exactly $2$. For the remaining even exponents, the previous lower bounds were of order $r2^r$. When $n=2m$ with $m\ge3$ odd, we prove the transfer inequality \[ A_n(H\oplus C_n^5)\ \ge\ 12\,A_n(H\oplus C_n)+8\,A_n(H\oplus C_m), \] where $A_n(G)$ is the maximal length of a sequence over $G$ without an $n$-term zero-sum subsequence and $H$ is any finite abelian group whose exponent divides $n$. The transfer extends a configuration of Elsholtz to twenty full cyclic fibers. Combined with a nine-point binary construction for $2m$-term zero-sums over $C_m^r$, it gives bases at least $2.0341$ that tend to $2.0394\ldots$; combined with a finite-field construction, it gives $s(C_6^r)\ge c\cdot 2.0491^r$. For exponents divisible by $4$ that are not powers of two, we obtain a base above two from a weighted random construction on the eighteen-point configuration of Wang and Zeng.
item.dc:creator: Krishnendu Bhowmick

item.title: Weak Unit Reducibility of the Eleventh Cyclotomic Field
item.description: arXiv:2611.15432v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the cyclotomic field $K_{11}=\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_{11})$ is unit reducible but not strongly unit reducible. So every nonzero principal fractional ideal of $K_{11}$ has a generator that is a shortest nonzero vector. For $I=h\mathcal{O}_{K_{11}}$, every shortest nonzero vector $\alpha\in I$ satisfies $N_{K_{11}/\mathbb{Q}}(\alpha/h)\in\{1,11\}$. The proof uses Sigrist's Hermite bound for cyclic forms and an averaging identity for cyclotomic units. For principal ideals in $K_{11}$, ideal-SVP and the shortest-generator problem are polynomial-time equivalent.
item.dc:creator: Yiyang Chang

item.title: Newforms as test vectors for representations of Saito-Kurokawa type
item.description: arXiv:2611.15483v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study irreducible (admissible) representations $\pi$ of the split group $G_n=SO(2n+1)$, both over finite and $p$-adic fields, which are distinguished for the (unramified) nonsplit form of $K_n=SO(2n)$ and for one more subgroup $H_n$. Over finite fields, $H_n$ is the split $SO(2n)$ while over $p$-adic fields it is the Gross-Tsai paramodular subgroup (of minimal level for $\pi$). These are all multiplicity one situations. With $0 \neq \ell_{n,K} \in {\rm Hom}_{K_n}(\pi_n,1)$ and $0 \neq v_{n,H} \in \pi_n^{H_n}$, both being one dimensional spaces, we are interested in the vanishing/nonvanishing of $|\ell_{n,K}(v_{n,H})|^2$. Appropriately normalized, this defines the notion of the correlation coefficient $c(\pi;H_n,K_n)$ of $H_n$ and $K_n$ in $G_n$ with respect to $\pi$. Via the theta correspondence between ${\rm SL}(2)$ (or ${\rm Mp}(2)$), we establish a bijection $\pi_n \leftrightarrow \pi_1$ between representations of $G_n$ and $G_1$ under consideration. Our main results then prove that $d_n c(\pi_n;H_n,K_n)$ is independent of the rank $n$, where $d_n =\dim \pi_n$ for finite fields and is defined in terms of the index of $H_n$ in the standard maximal compact subgroup of $G_n$ in the $p$-adic case. We also highlight a conjecture from [Ana25] on Legendre polynomials modulo $p$. Its truth will have the arithmetic consequence that over $\mathbb F_p$, given $\pi_1$, we can choose $u \in \mathbb F_p$ such that, in every rank $n$, all the correlation coefficients $c(\pi_n;H_n,u_nK_n u_n^{-1})$ are simultaneously nonzero and moreover they belong to $\mathbb Z_p^\times$ under any identification $\mathbb C \simeq \overline{\mathbb Q}_p$, where $u_n$ is a specific unipotent element in $G_n$ corresponding to $u$.
item.dc:creator: U. K. Anandavardhanan

item.title: Equidistribution of Hecke neighbours and continued fraction patterns
item.description: arXiv:2611.15558v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove uniform tightness of Hecke neighbours of any probability measure of positive entropy that is invariant and ergodic under the diagonal flow. As an application, we confirm a conjecture of Einsiedler concerning a homogeneous dynamics analogue of an equidistribution theorem of Johnson and Rudolph on the torus. We also obtain applications to continued-fraction patterns in arithmetic sequences and to the \(p\)-adic Littlewood conjecture. Our proof studies escape of mass using dynamics on the boundary of the Chabauty compactification of the space of lattices, together with averaging operators defined by leafwise measures along horospherical subgroups.
item.dc:creator: Menny Aka, Segev Gonen Cohen

item.title: An Empirical Square-Root Law for the Degree Discrepancy of Binary m-Sequences
item.description: arXiv:2611.15635v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $k\ge 2$, $N=2^k$, $M=N-1$ and let $\Delta(r)$ be the range, over all starting offsets, of the total-variation degree discrepancy of a length-$r$ window of a primitive binary linear feedback shift register (LFSR) of period $M$. Degree-discrepancy profiles for every $k\le 28$ support the scaling $\max_r \Delta(r)=\Theta(\sqrt{N})=\Theta(2^{k/2})$. The tabulated peaks are maxima on a discrete grid, hence lower bounds on the exhaustive maximum. The normalized peaks $d_k=\max_{r\in R_k}\Delta(r)/2^{k/2}$ oscillate between values near 1/2 and values that approach, but do not exceed, 1. The data suggest $\liminf d_k=1/2$ and $\limsup d_k\le 1$. We conjecture the same square-root law for the exhaustive maximum, with those normalized envelopes. A Brownian-bridge heuristic accounts for the square-root scale. The same profiles do not place the recorded maximizer at mid-path: after folding by the complement identity $\Delta(M-r)=\Delta(r)$, the median of $\min(\rho^*_k,1-\rho^*_k)$ is 0.35, and several $k$ (notably 16 and 28) peak on a short window. Mid-horizon $\Delta$ remains a large fraction of the peak, so the square-root scale can still come from a Brownian-bridge envelope. The same range has two readings of the starting offset: a pairing fragment in serial-knockout scheduling, and a change to the plaintext on an LFSR orbit. The location of the maximizer is not part of the conjecture. Open questions that separate the conjecture from a theorem are listed.
item.dc:creator: Joonas P\"a\"akk\"onen

item.title: Base Change Of Local Fundamental Group Schemes
item.description: arXiv:2611.15643v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, $K/k$ a field extension, $X$ a geometrically reduced connected scheme proper over $k$, and $x\in X(k)$. We study when the natural homomorphism $\pi^{Loc}(X_K,x_K)\rightarrow\pi^{Loc}(X,x)_K$ is an isomorphism. If $\mathcal C^{Loc}(X)$ is saturated, then it is an isomorphism for every algebraic extension $K/k$. If $\pi^{Loc}(X,x)$ is finite, then it is an isomorphism if $K/k$ is purely transcendental or $k$ is algebraically closed. Combining these results, if $\mathcal C^{Loc}(X)$ is saturated and $\pi^{Loc}(X,x)$ is finite, then the natural homomorphism $\pi^{Loc}(X_K,x_K)\rightarrow \pi^{Loc}(X,x)_K$ is an isomorphism. As an application, if $X_{\bar k}$ is smooth and rationally chain connected, then the natural homomorphism $\pi^{Loc}(X_K,x_K)\longrightarrow\pi^{Loc}(X,x)_K$ is an isomorphism.
item.dc:creator: Lingguang Li, Niantao Tian

item.title: Critical L-values and genus-zero Gromov--Witten invariants
item.description: arXiv:2611.15696v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish a period comparison for a two-dimensional rational Hodge summand of type $(3,0)+(0,3)$ in a smooth projective threefold over $\mathbb Q$ with $h^{3,0}=1$. Given an algebraic projector onto the summand and a correspondence whose action on the motive of a rational weight-four newform is nonzero after projection to the summand, restriction to the holomorphic de Rham lines identifies motivic morphisms with maps between these lines. Fixing rational generators of the holomorphic de Rham lines determines a unique isomorphism of homological motives. Its Betti realization then yields an exact relation between geometric periods and two critical modular $L$-values. For the Fermat sextic, we construct the correspondence over $\mathbb Q$ and compute its Betti and de Rham actions, determining the scale from algebraic traces and cup-product pairings. Critical-value evaluations and, under mirror comparison and explicit continuation hypotheses, a continued genus-zero Gromov--Witten partition identity follow as corollaries.
item.dc:creator: Wu-yen Chuang, Yi-Jing Tseng

item.title: Stable irrationality of quartic hypersurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.15702v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that a very general quartic hypersurface of any positive dimension over an uncountable algebraically closed field of characteristic different from 2 does not admit an integral decomposition of the diagonal, and in particular it is not stably rational.
item.dc:creator: Christian B\"ohning, Hans-Christian Graf von Bothmer, Alena Pirutka, Zhijia Zhang

item.title: A projective Calabi--Yau threefold in characteristic 5 non-liftable to characteristic 0
item.description: arXiv:2611.15943v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a smooth projective Calabi--Yau threefold $X_5$ over $\mathbb F_5$ with $b_3(X_5)=0$ and $b_2(X_5)=31$. Consequently, $X_5$ has no smooth proper lifting to characteristic zero, including over ramified bases. To our knowledge, this is the first smooth projective Calabi--Yau threefold with this property in characteristic $p>3$. The threefold is a crepant resolution of the Kummer quotient of the self-fiber product of a rational elliptic surface. We prove the vanishing of its third Betti number by semistable reduction and point counts. A birational double-octic model gives a direct obstruction to lifting to the ring of Witt vectors of length two, through an explicit inconsistent system of linear equations for the branch data. We also determine the Hodge and crystalline cohomology: the threefold is infinitesimally rigid, its crystalline cohomology is torsion-free, and its third de Rham cohomology vanishes. Its Hodge-de Rham spectral sequence has exactly two nonzero differentials, both of rank one on the second page.
item.dc:creator: Dominik Burek, Tymoteusz Chmiel, S{\l}awomir Cynk, Marcin Oczko

item.title: The Levitt--Yoccoz gasket: dynamics, Hausdorff dimension and norm exponent
item.description: arXiv:2611.15996v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In S.P.~Novikov's problem on plane sections of 3ply periodic surfaces, the author and I.\,A.~Dynnikov showed that, for the $\mu$-cube, the directions lying in no stability zone form the union of a fractal set $N$, the Levitt--Yoccoz gasket (projectively equivalent to the Rauzy gasket), and of its images under the sign changes of the coordinates. $N$ is the limit set of a parabolic projective iterated function system $P\Gamma_N$ generated by a semigroup $\Gamma_N\subset SL_3(\mathbb Z)$, and each zone is labelled by a primitive integer vector, its soul. We show that $N$ is the global attractor of $P\Gamma_N$ and that the chain graphs of $P\Gamma_N$ and its Hutchinson map consist of a single node. Building on the theorem of Jiao--Li--Pan--Xu and Jurga that $\dim_H N$ equals the affinity exponent of $\Gamma_N$, we prove $1.6853<\dim_HN=\dim_BN<1.6854$. For some class of cut-out gaskets $K$, we bound $\overline{\dim}_B K$ from both sides by the norm exponent $s_N(\Gamma)$. The norm exponent $s_N$ of $G_N$, the counting exponent of the souls, is Baragar's exponent of the Markoff--Hurwitz equation $x_1^2+x_2^2+x_3^2+x_4^2=ax_1x_2x_3x_4$. We prove $2.4411\le s_N\le2.4465$, improving Baragar's bounds, and $\frac23 s_N\le\dim_H N\le\frac12(1+s_N)$, which proves a conjecture by Gamburd, Magee and Ronan; and we show that the exponent of the equation in six variables exceeds $3$, answering a question of Baragar. For the three-dimensional Levitt--Yoccoz gasket $G\subset\mathbb RP^3$ we prove $2.74\le s_N(\Gamma_G)\le2.777$ and $\dim_H G\le2.3885$. Finally, for the renormalization flow of Avila, Hubert and Skripchenko, we show that the invariant measure they introduce is the Gibbs measure at the parameter $s_N$ and that $s_N$ is the maximal entropy per unit time of the return map, attained only by this measure. So, the diffusion exponent of their chaotic plane sections is less than 0.7766.
item.dc:creator: Roberto De Leo

item.title: Simple Length Multiplicity on X(n)
item.description: arXiv:2611.16078v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study multiplicity among lengths of simple closed geodesics on the principal congruence surfaces $X(n)=\Gamma(n)\backslash\mathbb{H}$. We show that for every $\varepsilon>0$ there are positive constants $n_\varepsilon,C_{\varepsilon}$ so that, for $n\ge n_\varepsilon$, there are at least $\exp((\frac{\pi^2}{12}-\varepsilon)n)$ simple closed geodesics on $X(n)$ of the same length $\ell<C_\varepsilon n$. We produce the same multiplicity for $\lambda$-length of simple arcs with distinct endpoints via the McShane identity, which is immediately relevant as the size of a McShane gap around such an arc is roughly the reciprocal square of its $\lambda$-length. Our method of proof relies on an independently interesting theorem about the McShane identity for $X(n)$: the total mass of the gaps of pants with two cusps tends to 1 as $n\to \infty$. We present a proof of this latter fact that relies on estimates for the speed of mixing provided by Selberg's 3/16-Theorem (discovered with the help of ChatGPT). We indicate several avenues for further investigation.
item.dc:creator: Jonah Gaster, Didac Martinez-Granado, Christopher-Lloyd Simon

item.title: Counting circles in Kleinian circle packings
item.description: arXiv:2611.16328v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a bounded Kleinian circle packing with symmetry group $\Gamma$, and let $N_{\mathcal{P}}(T)$ denote the number of circles in $\mathcal{P}$ of radius at least $T^{-1}$. We obtain an asymptotic formula for $N_{\mathcal{P}}(T)$ in which the eigenvalues of the Laplace operator below the continuous spectrum contribute a finite sum of main terms, with an error term having the same exponent as in the counting theorem of Lax--Phillips for $\Gamma$-orbits in $\mathbb H^3$.
item.dc:creator: Samuel C. Edwards

item.title: Matrix Waring Problem in finite fields with coefficients from $\mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{F}_p)$
item.description: arXiv:2611.16651v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $k$ be a fixed positive integer and $p$ be an odd prime such that $\gcd(p-1,k)=1$. For sufficiently large primes $p$, we show that the equation $AX^k+BY^k=C$ has solutions $X,Y \in \mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{F}_p)$, where $A$ and $B$ are fixed matrices in $\mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{F}_p)$, and $C$ is a fixed matrix in $\mathrm{M}(2,\mathbb{F}_p).$ Our proof relies on Fourier analysis over $\mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{F}_p).$
item.dc:creator: Sutirtha Datta, Sourav Ghosh, Aniruddha Maji, Antara Manik

item.title: Modular representations of reductive $p$-adic groups and the kernel of the trace map
item.description: arXiv:2611.16847v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The trace map of a finite group gives a perfect duality between conjugacy classes and irreducible complex representations. For reductive $p$-adic groups, an analogous duality holds due to the classical work of Bernstein, Deligne and Kazhdan. In this paper, we study this trace map for modular representations of reductive $p$-adic groups in characteristic $\ell\ne p$. The failure of the duality is measured by the kernel of the trace map on the cocenter of the ``big Hecke algebra''. Our main theorem expresses this kernel in terms of corresponding kernels for finite-dimensional Hecke algebras associated with normalizers of parahoric subgroups in suitable central quotients of Levi subgroups, reducing a problem on infinite-dimensional algebras to finite-dimensional ones. We also show that projective representations provide a natural complementary subspace on the compact part of the cocenter. For affine Hecke algebras, we prove the naive-kernel conjecture over algebraically closed fields of arbitrary characteristic and for arbitrary compatible nonzero parameters, including unequal parameters and roots of unity.
item.dc:creator: Xuhua He

item.title: Rohrbach's Conjecture for Finite Groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.16938v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Rohrbach's conjecture holds for finite groups. In fact, there is an absolute constant $C$ such that, for every finite group $G$, every positive integer $h$, and all nonnegative real numbers $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_h$ with $\alpha_1+\cdots+\alpha_h=1$, there are subsets $A_1,\ldots,A_h\subseteq G$ satisfying \[ G=A_1\cdots A_h, \qquad |A_1|\leq |G|^{\alpha_1}, \qquad |A_i|\leq C|G|^{\alpha_i}\quad(2\leq i\leq h). \] Consequently, for every $h$ there is a constant $c_h$ such that every finite group $G$ has a subset $A$ with \[ A^h=G\qquad\text{and}\qquad |A|\leq c_h|G|^{1/h}. \]
item.dc:creator: Yong Yang

item.title: A completely decomposable modular Jacobian of dimension $1777$
item.description: arXiv:2611.16963v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We exhibit a congruence subgroup $\Gamma\subset\operatorname{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ of level $120$ and index $23040$ whose modular curve $X_\Gamma$ has genus $1777$ and whose Jacobian is isogenous over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ to a product of elliptic curves. This surpasses the previous record of a completely decomposable complex Jacobian of dimension $1297$ found by Ekedahl and Serre in $1993$.
item.dc:creator: Robert Auffarth

item.title: Dimension drop for superlevel sets of the uniform Littlewood constant
item.description: arXiv:2611.17189v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For $(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^2$ and $Q\ge 1$, set $F_Q(x,y)=Q\min_{1\le q\le Q}\lVert qx\rVert\lVert qy\rVert$, where $q$ ranges over positive integers and $\lVert\cdot\rVert$ denotes distance to the nearest integer. The set on which the uniform Littlewood constant $L=\limsup_{Q\to\infty}F_Q$ is positive has full Hausdorff dimension. We prove that for every fixed $c>0$ the superlevel set $\{L\ge c\}$ has Hausdorff dimension strictly less than two. More precisely, the Lebesgue measure of $\{(x,y)\in[0,1]^2:F_Q(x,y)\ge c\}$ is $O_c(Q^{-\kappa(c)})$ for some $\kappa(c)>0$ and all $Q\ge 2$. The proof combines large deviations for one diagonal action on the space of unimodular lattices with effective equidistribution of expanding horospheres for another.
item.dc:creator: Shahriar Mirzadeh

item.title: Forbidden subset sums in a linear range: an inverse theorem and the Erd\H{o}s-Graham irregularity problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.17205v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For $c>0$ let $f_c(n)$ be the largest size of a set $A\subseteq\{1,\dots,\lfloor cn\rfloor\}$ such that $n$ is not a sum of distinct elements of $A$. Erd\H{o}s and Graham asked whether $f_c(n)$ depends on $n$ in an irregular way (Erd\H{o}s Problem \#361). We prove that $f_c(n)=\lfloor cn\rfloor-\lceil n/2\rceil$ for $c\ge 1$, while for $0<c<1$ the ratio $f_c(n)/n$ has $\limsup$ equal to $c/2$, attained along odd $n$, and, along the integers $n$ whose least non-divisor equals a prime power $q$, tends to \[ \max\Bigl\{\frac cq,\; c-\frac12+\frac{1-c}{q}\Bigr\} \qquad\text{whenever } 2^{q-2}\min\{c,1-c\}\le 1 . \] Consequently $f_c(n)/n$ converges if and only if $c\ge1$; for $0<c<1$ it has at least two limit points, and arbitrarily many as $c\to0^+$ or $c\to1^-$. For $c=1/2$ the set of limit points is exactly $\{1/6,1/4\}$. The upper bounds follow from an inverse theorem of independent interest: if $s\ge1$, $q$ is the least positive integer not dividing $s$, and $\varepsilon>0$, then every $A\subseteq\{1,\dots,E\}$ with $|A|\ge E/q+\varepsilon T$ has a subset summing to $sT$, uniformly for all sufficiently large $T$ and all $E\le sT/2^{q-2}$. For $s=2$, this extends Alon's theorem on subsets of $\{1,\dots,N\}$ with no subset sum equal to $2N$. The results for $c\ge1$ and the $\limsup$, as well as the limits and the inverse theorem for $q\in\{2,3\}$, have been formalized and machine-checked in the Lean~4 proof assistant.
item.dc:creator: Mateo Matijasevick

item.title: On properties of the generalized Davenport Expansion
item.description: arXiv:2204.00854v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the continuity properties of a generalized Davenport Fourier expansion we recently discovered, by imposing conditions on the coefficients. We also put our expansion into perspective from the position of Appell sequences.
item.dc:creator: Alexander E. Patkowski

item.title: Local duality theorems for commutative algebraic groups
item.description: arXiv:2305.08699v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let k be a non-archimedean local field and let G be a commutative algebraic k-group that contains no nontrivial unipotent subgroups if car k=0. Given any presentation of G as an extension of commutative algebraic k-groups E: 0 --> L --> G --> A --> 0, where L is affine and A is an abelian variety, we establish Pontryagin duality theorems that relate the fppf cohomology groups of G (equipped with the extension structure E) to the hypercohomology groups of the dual of G in the truncated derived category D^{[-1,0]}(k_{fppf}). These results have applications (to be discussed elsewhere) to certain generalizations of Lichtenbaum-van Hamel duality to a class of non-smooth proper k-varieties.
item.dc:creator: Cristian D. Gonzalez-Aviles

item.title: General elementary methods meeting elementary properties of correlations
item.description: arXiv:2309.17101v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This is a kind of survey on properties of correlations of two very general arithmetic functions, from the point of view of {\it Ramanujan expansions}. In fact, our previous papers on these links had, as a focus, the "{\it Ramanujan coefficients}" of these correlations and the resulting "{\it R.e.e.f.}", i.e., {\it Ramanujan exact explicit formula}. This holds under a variety of sufficient conditions, mainly under two conditions of convergence involving correlation's {\it \lq \lq Eratosthenes Transform\rq \rq}, namely what we call {\it Delange Hypothesis} (DH) and {\it Wintner Assumption} (WA) (the former implying the latter). We proved, on Hardy-Ramanujan Journal, the {\it Hardy-Littlewood Conjecture} on {\it $2k-$twin primes}, in particular, from (DH) (implying convergence of the Ramanujan expansion, whence {\it R.e.e.f.}); then, we gave a more general proof, from (WA), again {\it entailing the R.e.e.f.}, but from another method of summation for {\it Ramanujan expansions}, that we detailed in arXiv, "On Ramanujan smooth expansions for a general arithmetic function". There we also started to introduce local Ramanujan coefficients. Which we deepen here, entailing a new conditional proof of quoted H-L Conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Coppola

item.title: Families of two dimensional modular $(\varphi,\Gamma)$-modules
item.description: arXiv:2405.17133v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $F/{\mathbb Q}_p$ be a finite unramified extension, let $k$ be a finite extension of the residue field of $F$. We provide explicit constructions of integral structures for all rank two \'{e}tale Lubin-Tate $(\varphi,{\mathcal O}_F^{\times})$-modules over $k$. We construct algebraic families of such integral structures and show that these comprehensively reflect the degeneration behaviour of $(\varphi,{\mathcal O}_F^{\times})$-modules. These results reveal new combinatorial structures of the moduli stack of $(\varphi,{\mathcal O}_F^{\times})$-modules, and allow us, in particular, to rederive the fact that the Serre weights assigned to a two dimensional ${\rm Gal}(\overline{F}/F)$-representation over $k$ can be read off from the geometry of the stack.
item.dc:creator: Elmar Gro{\ss}e-Kl\"onne

item.title: On the Stieltjes Approximation Error to the Logarithmic Integral
item.description: arXiv:2406.12152v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the approximation errors $\varepsilon(x)=\operatorname{li}_{*}(x)-\operatorname{li}(x)$ and $\varepsilon_{S}(x)=\operatorname{li}_{S}(x)-\operatorname{li}(x)$ arising from the classical Stieltjes--van Boven and pure Stieltjes asymptotic expansions of the logarithmic integral, respectively. Our analysis establishes a top-down reduction based on the discrete error sequence $\varepsilon_n=\varepsilon(e^n)$ and its localized partial variations, for which we derive new, unconditional analytic bounds. By developing precise integral representations for these error increments and establishing sharp, fully explicit upper and lower estima-tes for the underlying kernel integrals, we obtain uniform bounds valid for every integer $n\geq 1$. These discrete results are subsequently lifted to the real domain to provide comprehensive estimates for all real $x\geq e$. In particular, we prove that $\varepsilon(x) = \frac{1}{3} \sqrt{2\pi/\log x} + O(1/\log x)$ as $x \to \infty$. Furthermore, we deploy these continuous bounds to uncover the fine structural behavior of the pure Stieltjes expansion, demonstrating that $|\varepsilon_{S}(x)| = \sqrt{2\pi}\,|1/3-\alpha|/\sqrt{\log x} + O(1/\log x)$ as $x\to\infty$, where $n=\lfloor\log x\rfloor$ and $\alpha=\log x-n$. This establishes a novel and explicit asymptotic description of the absolute pure Stieltjes error, fully capturing its non-trivial oscillatory dependence on the fractional part of the logarithm.
item.dc:creator: Jonatan Gomez

item.title: A full-rank subgroup of Bloch Groups of CM Fields
item.description: arXiv:2507.05792v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This article generalizes the result of Burns et al (2022), to find an algorithm to find some elements generating a full-rank subgroup of the torsion-free part of Bloch group of a certain CM number field, and compute the rank of it.
item.dc:creator: Wenhuan Huang

item.title: An interpolation of Bradley's sum formula
item.description: arXiv:2508.13254v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The sum formula for $q$-multiple zeta values is a well-known relation. In this paper, we present its generalization for the $q$-multiple zeta function.
item.dc:creator: Anju Yokoi

item.title: A Dynamical N\'eron--Ogg--Shafarevich Criterion via Orbital Arboreal Representations
item.description: arXiv:2510.23097v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $K$ be a non-archimedean local field and $\varphi : \mathbb{P}^1 \to \mathbb{P}^1$ a rational endomorphism of degree $d \geq 2$ over $K$. In the tame case ($p \nmid d$), we show that strict good reduction is equivalent to the existence of a nonempty Zariski open subset $U_k \subset \mathbb{P}^1_k \setminus \mathrm{PC}(\widetilde{\varphi})$ over which the canonical residual morphism is finite \'etale of degree $d$. The criterion separates two complementary local invariants of a normalized integral lift: $\mathrm{Res}(F,G)$ controls residual degree drop, while the fiber discriminants $\mathrm{Disc}(F_{n,x})$ control \'etaleness of the residual fibers once full residual degree is ensured. Consequently, for every finite $x \in \mathcal{O}_K$ with $\bar{x} \in U_k$, the extensions $K(X_n(x))/K$ are unramified for all $n \geq 1$. We introduce the orbital preimage tree $T_{O^+(x)} = \varinjlim_n X_\infty(\varphi^n(x))$, the colimit in $G_K$-sets along the forward orbit, and the orbital arboreal Galois image $\mathcal{G}_{O^+(x)} = \mathrm{Im}(G_K \to \mathrm{Aut}(T_{O^+(x)}))$. On the forward-invariant safe locus $U_k^{\mathrm{safe}} = \bigcap_{m \geq 0} \widetilde{\varphi}^{-m}(U_k)$, strict good reduction is captured by the bijectivity of the orbital reduction map $X_n(x_m) \to \widetilde{X}_n(\bar{x}_m)$. This canonical orbit-invariant framework connects with arboreal Galois representations (Boston-Jones, Jones, and others) and yields pointwise and orbit-level reformulations. Explicit examples over $\mathbb{Q}_p$ illustrate the criterion.
item.dc:creator: J. Rogelio P\'erez-Buend\'ia

item.title: Effective existence of primitive k-normal elements via affine spaces
item.description: arXiv:2510.26972v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$ be the finite field with $q^n$ elements. An element $\alpha \in \mathbb{F}_{q^n}$ is $k$-normal over $\mathbb{F}_q$ if $\alpha$ and its conjugates span an $\mathbb{F}_q$-subspace of dimension $n-k$. It is known that, for $q$ larger than a constant $c(n)$, a primitive $k$-normal element exists if and only if there exists a $k$-normal element free of binomials, but $c(n)$ is not explicit. We count the $k$-normal elements in affine subspaces of the form $\beta+\ker L_h$ and show that, when $h$ is an irreducible factor of the $\mathbb{F}_q$-order of $\beta$, all but at most one of them are $k$-normal. We also show that, when $\beta$ is free of binomials, these affine subspaces have degree $n$, so that character sum estimates over affine spaces apply to them. Combining these facts with a sieve, we make the equivalence above effective, with explicit lower bounds on $q$. As an application, we compute these bounds for $5\le n\le 8$ and give a complete characterization of the existence of primitive $k$-normal elements in $\mathbb{F}_{q^6}$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$.
item.dc:creator: Josimar J. R. Aguirre, Sarah F. M. Mazzini, Victor G. L. Neumann

item.title: A Dynamical Lifting Problem For Additive Polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2604.08795v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a dynamical analogue of the lifting problem for Galois covers of algebraic curves and find a negative solution for the collection of separable additive and semi-additive polynomials over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$. We also explicitly compute the dimension of the space of linear conjugacy classes in $\mathcal{M}_{p^m}(\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p)$ which contain additive or semi-additive polynomials providing explicit counterexamples to Thurston Rigidity in positive characteristic.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Tedeschi

item.title: Power-integral matrices over number fields: the Drazin inverse, pseudo-determinant, and numerical semigroups
item.description: arXiv:2606.30876v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate matrices with entries in a number field such that some positive power has all its entries in the corresponding ring of integers. Our work generalizes previous results in several directions and we find applications to numerical semigroups.
item.dc:creator: Theo Chinn, Junshu Feng, Stephan Ramon Garcia, Hechun Zhang

item.title: Reduction Types of Genus 2 Curves
item.description: arXiv:2607.07558v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Tate produced a table for elliptic curves over local fields that beautifully summarises their arithmetic invariants in terms of the Kodaira type. We present an analogous set of tables for curves of genus 2. The invariants addressed include: reduction type of the minimal regular model, reduction type of the minimal regular model with normal crossings, N\'eron component group of the Jacobian, conductor exponent, valuation of the discriminant of a minimal Weierstrass model, and cluster pictures.
item.dc:creator: Edwina Aylward, Lilybelle Cowland Kellock, Vladimir Dokchitser, Elvira Lupoian

item.title: The motivic Selmer scheme of the thrice-punctured line
item.description: arXiv:2608.11509v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $X = \mathbb{P}^1 \smallsetminus \{0,1,\infty\}$ be the thrice-punctured line over a ring of $S$-integers $\mathcal{O}_{K,S}$ in a number field $K$. For any quotient $\pi_1^{\mathrm{mot}}(X,0) \twoheadrightarrow \Pi$ of Deligne--Goncharov's motivic fundamental group there is an associated Selmer scheme which parametrises $\Pi$-torsors with a mixed Tate motive structure. We give several descriptions of the motivic Selmer scheme which make it amenable to computations, using $\mathbb{G}_m$-equivariant cocycles of algebraic groups, Lie algebras, and complete Hopf algebras. We prove that the Selmer scheme is isomorphic to an affine space $\mathbb{A}^N_{\mathbb{Q}}$, and we construct coordinates realising this isomorphism. This is a key ingredient for making the motivic Chabauty--Kim method explicit in a general setting, without restrictions on the base field or the choice of fundamental group quotient.
item.dc:creator: Martin L\"udtke

item.title: Squarefree polynomials with missing digits
item.description: arXiv:2608.17892v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish an asymptotic formula for squarefree polynomials over a finite field whose coefficients are in $\{0,1\}$. This resolves a function-field analogue of a conjecture of Erd\H{o}s, Mauduit and S\'ark\"ozy. More generally, we estimate the probability of a polynomial $\sum \varepsilon_it^i$ being squarefree, where $\varepsilon_i$ are random variables sampled according to measures on $\mathbb{F}_q$.
item.dc:creator: Naomi Bazlov

item.title: The average number of rational preperiodic points of polynomials over $\mathbb{Q}$
item.description: arXiv:2608.29383v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $M_d(X)$ denote the average number of rational preperiodic points among degree-$d$ polynomials over $\mathbb{Q}$ with vanishing $z^{d-1}$ coefficient, constant term $1$, and height at most $X$. We prove that, for every integer $d\ge2$, $M_d(X) \sim \gamma_d X^{-1}$ for an explicit constant $\gamma_d>0$. For $d\ge4$, the error term is $O_{d,\varepsilon}(X^{-2+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$; for $d=3$ the error term is $O(X^{-3/2})$; and for $d=2$ the error term is $O(X^{-3/2}\log X)$.
item.dc:creator: Jungin Lee

item.title: On $t$-sumfree sequences
item.description: arXiv:2609.16843v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we explore the world of $t$-sumfree sequences, primarily for $t=2$ and $t=3$. Starting with $t$ increasing positive integers, build an infinite sequence by choosing as the next entry the least positive integer that is not the sum of $t$ distinct previous values. The main open problem concerns the question of the conjectured ultimate periodicity of these sequences. We formulate a sufficient condition to prove that a conjectured preperiod and period are correct. We also prove periodicity for a considerable subclass of 2-sumfree and of 3-sumfree sequences. Finally, we present the results of extensive computations on 3-sumfree sequences.
item.dc:creator: Daan van Berkel, Wieb Bosma

item.title: The existence and uniqueness of magic-faced hypercubes, and applications to Khajuraho most-perfect magic squares, cubes, and hypercubes
item.description: arXiv:2609.26762v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A $\textit{magic-lined hypercube}$ (or, simply, $\textit{magic hypercube}$) of order $k$ and dimension $n$ is an arrangement of the numbers $1,\dots,k^n$ in a $k\times\cdots\times k$ ($n$-fold) grid such that every line of $k$ numbers parallel to a coordinate axis has the same magic sum. While such hypercubes exist for every order $k\ge 3$ and every dimension $n$, no magic-lined hypercube of order $2$ exists in any dimension $n\ge 2$. For hypercubes of order $2$, we thus relax the magic condition from lines to two-dimensional faces or planes. We call an arrangement of the numbers $1,\dots,2^n$ in a $2\times\cdots\times2$ ($n$-fold) grid \emph{magic-faced} if every $2\times2$ face has the same magic sum. We prove that a magic-faced hypercube of order $2$ exists in every dimension $n\ge0$, and that it is unique up to a certain natural set of transformations of size $2^n(n+1)!$ when $n$ is even and $2^n n\cdot n!$ when $n$ is odd. As an application, we recover and generalize the classical $4\times4$ Khajuraho magic square, give a new, conceptual answer to a question of Coxeter on the group acting on the $384$ ``most-perfect" $4\times4$ magic squares, and extend the picture to higher dimensions. In particular, we prove that, in dimension $n$, these most-perfect hypercubes form a single orbit under a certain natural action of the Weyl group $W(B_{2n})$.
item.dc:creator: Manjul Bhargava

item.title: Shimura Reciprocity for Real Quadratic Fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.02419v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The purpose of this note is to give conditional explicit formulas for the Galois action on real multiplication values of the Shintani--Faddeev modular cocycle. We assume the order 1 abelian Stark conjecture for real quadratic fields. We conclude this note by presenting our own conjecture about the Galois action. Numerical evidence for this conjecture is provided by the algorithm described in \hyperref[sec4]{Section 4} and the attached code.
