item.dc:creator: Joseph DiCapua

item.title: Coefficient arithmetic and Mellin moments of the Rogers-Ramanujan continued fraction
item.description: arXiv:2610.10578v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the signs of logarithmic coefficients associated with the Rogers-Ramanujan continued fraction. An explicit criterion involving a finite product determines whether all coefficients in an arithmetic progression are negative or both signs occur with positive natural density. On the sets $n=5^a m$, $5\nmid m$, negative coefficients occur with positive relative density $\delta_a^-$ at every fixed $a$. If $m_a$ is the least such $m$, we prove that both $5^{-a}\log\log(1/\delta_a^-)$ and $5^{-a}\log\log m_a$ tend to $5\log\phi/(12e^\gamma)$, where $\phi=(1+\sqrt5)/2$ and $\gamma$ is Euler's constant. These are leading double-logarithmic asymptotics, obtained from classical results on additive and multiplicative functions. Coefficient formulas also give irrationality and nonvanishing, determine the poles and residues of generating functions for normalized Mellin moments, and imply that these generating functions are not D-finite. We conclude with applications to integrals involving zeta, Dirichlet $L$, and cusp-form $L$-functions.
item.dc:creator: K. Srinivasa Raghava

item.title: Solutions of $x_1^2+x_2^2-x_3^2=D$ with small $x_3$: a spectral approach
item.description: arXiv:2610.15706v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We count the integral solutions of $x_1^2+x_2^2-x_3^2=D$ with $|x_3|$ of size at most $M$, for $M$ smaller than $\sqrt D$, using a smooth weight $\Phi(x_3/M)$. Such solutions correspond to binary quadratic forms of discriminant $D$, and hence to geodesics in the hyperbolic plane. Under this correspondence, $x_3$ is small exactly when the geodesic passes close to the point $i$. We count these geodesics by the spectral theory of automorphic forms. Throughout, $\theta=7/64$ is the Kim-Sarnak exponent. For non-square $D=f^2D_0$, with $D_0$ a fundamental discriminant, the geodesics are closed. We obtain an asymptotic formula with error $O(D^{\varepsilon}f^{1+\theta}D_0^{2/3}M^{-1/2})$. The main inputs are the formulas of Duke-Imamoglu-Toth and Baruch-Mao for cycle integrals, the cubic moment bounds of Young and of Andersen-Wu, and a Hecke relation which reduces everything to the fundamental discriminant $D_0$. For $D\equiv 5 \bmod 8$ this counts all solutions, and the range $M\ge D^{1/2-1/1332}$ of Friedlander and Iwaniec improves to $M\ge D^{4/9+\varepsilon}$. For square $D=n^2$ the geodesics run from cusp to cusp, and Hecke theory reduces them to the single geodesic from $0$ to $\infty$. For every $n$ and both parities of $x_3$ we obtain an asymptotic formula with error $O(n^{1+\theta+\varepsilon}M^{-1/2})$, which is non-trivial for $M\ge n^{71/96+\varepsilon}$. This improves the range $n^{5/6+\varepsilon}$ of the elementary method and confirms the corrected main term of the author's earlier work. This paper was written in collaboration with Claude (Opus 5.5, High; Fable 5.2 in the final stage), an AI model developed by Anthropic.
item.dc:creator: Stephan Baier

item.title: 48 unknowns for Hilbert's tenth problem over the rationals
item.description: arXiv:2610.20691v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recently, Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the field $\mathbb Q$ of rational numbers was solved negatively by OpenAI based on a five-contact height estimate and a pole-parity construction. In this paper, we prove further that there is no algorithm to decide for any polynomial $P(x_1,\ldots,x_{48})$ with integer coefficients whether the equation $P(x_1,\ldots,x_{48})=0$ has solutions with $x_1,\ldots,x_{48}\in\mathbb Q$.
item.dc:creator: Zhi-Wei Sun

item.title: A number field extension of Ramanujan's identity and its integral representation via the generalized Riemann $\Xi$-function
item.description: arXiv:2610.21800v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: On pages 219--220 of Ramanujan's Lost Notebook appears an intriguing modular transformation whose integral representation is expressed in terms of the Riemann $\Xi$-function. In this paper, we establish a number field analogue of this identity. We also obtain an integral representation for the transformation formula associated with the functional equation of the higher power of the Dedekind zeta function recently studied by the present author and Maji. Interestingly, we recover Hardy's integral representation of the well-known Jacobi theta relation involving the Riemann $\Xi$-function. We further obtain a number-field analogue of the extended Ramanujan--Koshliakov formula established by Dixit.
item.dc:creator: Diksha Rani Bansal

item.title: Variation of Shafarevich-Tate groups in Hida families
item.description: arXiv:2610.22226v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathbf{f}$ be a Hida family of cusp forms over a standard (power series) Iwasawa algebra. We determine the pseudo-isomorphism class of the big Shafarevich-Tate group attached to $\mathbf{f}$ over a suitable imaginary quadratic field by describing all its higher Fitting ideals; this description is given in terms of the universal Kolyvagin system of Howard's big Heegner points. As a second contribution, we study the variation of the structure of the Shafarevich-Tate groups of the classical specializations of $\mathbf{f}$.
item.dc:creator: Enrico Da Ronche, Matteo Longo, Stefano Vigni, Francesco Zerman

item.title: Metric Poissonian Pair Correlation Property Part 1: The Case \(n+\log n\)
item.description: arXiv:2610.22836v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that $(\alpha(n+\log n))_{n\ge1}$ has Poissonian pair correlation for Lebesgue almost every real $\alpha$. This solves a Problem posed by Aistleitner, El-Baz and Munsch [Open Problem 2, Geom. Funct. Anal. 2021].
item.dc:creator: Bo Tan, Zhen Zhang, Qing-Long Zhou

item.title: Sharp spherical $L^p\to L^4$ extension estimates over finite fields in odd dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.29664v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $q$ be an odd prime power, let $d\ge3$ be odd, and let $S_j=\{\xi\in \mathbb F_q^d:\xi_1^2+\cdots+\xi_d^2=j\}$, where $j\ne 0$. We prove the sharp extension estimate ${L^{4(d+1)/(3d+1)}(S_j, d\sigma)\to L^4(\mathbb F_q^d,dc)}$ whenever $\eta_q((-1)^{(d-1)/2}j)=-1$, where $\eta_q$ is the quadratic character. This confirms the odd-dimensional spherical extension conjecture of Koh, Pham, and Vinh over every finite field of odd characteristic. Together with the known estimate in the complementary sign class, this determines the sharp ${L^p\to{L^4}}$ extension range for all nonzero-radius spheres in odd dimensions. We also apply the endpoint estimate to obtain sufficient conditions for the unique recovery of sparse signals from incomplete Fourier data.
item.dc:creator: Thang Pham, Boqing Xue

item.title: Geometric progressions in distance sets in odd dimensions over prime fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.34758v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For $E\subset\mathbb{F}_p^d$, let $\Delta(E)=\{Q_d(x-y):x,y\in E\}$, where $Q_d(z)=z_1^2+\cdots+z_d^2$. We introduce and study the problem of the existence of nondegenerate three-term geometric progressions in the distance set $\Delta(E)$ when $d$ is odd. Let $M_{GP,d}(p)$ be the largest size of a set whose distance set contains no such progression. For every prime $p\geq7$ and every integer $m\geq0$, we prove \[ p^mM_{GP,1}(p)\leq M_{GP,2m+1}(p) \leq4p^mM_{GP,1}(p). \] For all sufficiently large primes $p$, we also prove \[ p^{m+\frac{7}{26}}\leq M_{GP,2m+1}(p) \leq Cp^{m+\frac{16}{25}}, \] where $C$ is an absolute positive constant.
item.dc:creator: Thang Pham, Dung The Tran, Boqing Xue

item.title: Shifted convolutions of divisor functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.40439v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish the leading asymptotic for the shifted correlations of divisor functions.
item.dc:creator: Miguel N. Walsh

item.title: Harper's beyond square-root conjecture for random matrices
item.description: arXiv:2611.09753v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a Haar unitary matrix $U_N$ of size $N$, we prove that the first absolute moment of $\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{Sym}^k U_N)$ tends to zero as $\min(N,k)\to\infty$. This settles the random matrix version of Harper's beyond square-root conjecture formulated by Wang and Xu, with no restriction on $k/N$. The proof is elementary and self-contained, combining exact weighted trace moments with a Gaussian change of measure. It also connects the result to the critical chaos model studied by Soundararajan and Zaman, also known as holomorphic multiplicative chaos.
item.dc:creator: William Verreault, Max Wenqiang Xu

item.title: On Rankin Invariants of Ideal Lattices
item.description: arXiv:2611.11190v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Rankin constant $\gamma_{n,k}$ measures the largest discriminant of a densest rank $k$ sublattice of a lattice in $\R^n$ over all such lattices of rank $n$ and their exact values are mostly open. For a general lattice $L\subset \R^n$ of rank $n$, the problem of determining its Rankin invariant $\gamma_{n,k}(L)$ is to find the discriminant of such a densest sublattice. There are no general formulas to compute the discriminant of any arbitrary rank $k$ sublattice. This paper specializes to the case of ideal lattices arising from ideals of number fields, and provides two approaches to study Rankin constants: first, we propose a systematic approach to approximate the minimum discriminant by introducing subideal lattices and proving a closed-form formula to compute $\gamma^{ideal}_{n,k}(L)$, the ideal Rankin invariant of the ideal lattice. Subsequently, we establish necessary conditions on the underlying number field for the existence of an ideal lattice admitting an optimal subideal lattice with a prescribed minimum discriminant. Secondly, we consider ideal lattices with arbitrary sublattices. We improve the current known bounds of the Rankin constants $\gamma_{5,2}$, $\gamma_{7,2}$ and $\gamma_{9,2},\gamma_{9,3},\gamma_{9,4}$, and provide an algebraic construction of the lattice that was used in these dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Xiang Chew, Fr\'ed\'erique Oggier

item.title: Nontrivial Zeros of the Riemann Zeta Function and Its Derivative
item.description: arXiv:2611.12438v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function lie at the heart of analytic number theory. Through the explicit formulas, they govern the distribution of prime numbers: the closer all nontrivial zeros lie to the critical line $\Re(s)=\frac12$, the more uniformly the primes are distributed. The Riemann Hypothesis-asserting that all nontrivial zeros satisfy $\Re(s)=\frac12$-is equivalent to the optimal error bound $O(\sqrt{x}\log x)$ in the Prime Number Theorem. Beyond number theory, the zeros of $\zeta(s)$ and its derivative $\zeta'(s)$ are deeply intertwined: the horizontal distribution of $\zeta'$-zeros near the critical line encodes information about the spacing of consecutive $\zeta$-zeros. This paper establishes some results concerning the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function.
item.dc:creator: Chuancun Yin, Xianghua Zhao, Zuolu Hao, Zhongyang Sun

item.title: An asymptotic formula for primes of the form $u^2+v^2+1$
item.description: arXiv:2611.12467v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove Motohashi's conjecture on primes of the form $u^2+v^2+1$, with Iwaniec's corrected constant. Let $b$ denote the characteristic function of the positive integers representable as a sum of two squares. Then, as $x\to\infty$, \[ \sum_{p\le x}b(p-1) =\kappa\Spr\frac{x}{(\log x)^{3/2}} +O\!\left(\frac{x}{(\log x)^{3/2}\sqrt{\log\log x}}\right), \] where $\kappa$ is the Landau--Ramanujan constant and $\Spr=\prod_{p\equiv3\,({\rm mod}\,4)}\bigl(1-1/(p(p-1))\bigr)$. The proof combines auxiliary prime factors with a mean square estimate for bilinear sums. We obtain the minor arc bound through harmonic switching and high moments, replacing arithmetic divisibility conditions by independent projective lines. We remove the auxiliary weights using Selberg's sieve.
item.dc:creator: Yujiao Jiang, Yuk-Kam Lau, Guangshi L\"u

item.title: Asymptotically good codes from Siegel modular varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.14125v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct asymptotically good codes by evaluating Siegel modular forms at superspecial points on congruence towers of Siegel modular varieties. For every genus $g\ge2$ and every fixed weight $w\ge g+1$, the construction gives such a family in sufficiently large characteristic, over a finite field which is independent of the level of the tower. The towers can be chosen so that this field is $\mathbb{F}_{p^2}$. We give an explicit lower bound for the asymptotic rate. The lower bound for the relative minimum distance follows from the Pieri formula on the space of flags in the Hodge bundle and an intersection argument along its strata. We also prove that, for $p\ge5$ and $0\le w\le p+1$, the kernel of evaluation in every genus consists precisely of the multiples of the ordinary Hasse invariant. For $g=2,3$, the geometry of the supersingular locus gives explicit bounds for the relative minimum distance and recovery sets whose sizes are bounded independently of the level.
item.dc:creator: Yota Maeda

item.title: Symmetric compatibility of theta structures, with applications to change of level and isogenies
item.description: arXiv:2504.21058v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $m,n,d >1$ be integers such that $n=md$ and let $(B, \mathscr{M}, \Theta\_{\mathscr{M}})$ be a marked abelian variety of level $m$ over a field of odd characteristic. We study the theta structures of level $n$ for $\mathscr{M}^d$, and the theta structures on the abelian varieties $d$-isogenous to $B$, which are compatible with $\Theta\_{\mathscr{M}}$. When $d$ is odd and coprime to $m$, they correspond to the isotropic subgroups of $B[n]$, and this correspondence underlies the known algorithms in theta coordinates. In general, this is no longer true. We introduce the notion of symmetric compatibility of a torsion point with a symmetric level subgroup, and we show that a subgroup of $B[n]$ isomorphic to $(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^g$ comes from a compatible theta structure if and only if it is isotropic and all its points are symmetric compatible. We extend to every $d$ Mumford's notion of compatible pairs of theta structures, defined by Mumford for $d=2$, and prove that it is equivalent to our notion, which can be tested on theta coordinates; we also describe exactly the remaining ambiguity, which explains the sign choices met when the duplication formula is used to change the level. As applications, we obtain change of level and isogeny algorithms without assuming that $d$ is odd and coprime to $m$, using $O(n^{3g} \log(d))$ and $O(n^{2g} \log(d))$ operations in the base field respectively. In particular, they give change of level algorithms for even $d$, and $2$-isogenies in level $4$ theta coordinates with an explicit control of the theta structure of the codomain.
item.dc:creator: Antoine Dequay (IRMAR), David Lubicz (DGA.MI,IRMAR)

item.title: Diophantine equations in matrix rings and semirings
item.description: arXiv:2507.15265v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For every fixed positive integer $n$, we prove that it is undecidable whether a single noncommutative polynomial equation with scalar integer coefficients has a solution in $M_n(\mathbb N)$ or in $M_n(\mathbb Z)$. An integral range calculation for central polynomials yields a common reduction from integer Diophantine equations; the single-equation and finite-system problems are computably enumerable complete. The same polynomials have exact range $\mathbb Q I_n$ on rational, even nonnegative rational, arguments. Consequently, the single-equation and finite-system problems over $M_n(\mathbb Q)$ are computably many-one equivalent to Hilbert's tenth problem over $\mathbb Q$, unconditionally. The rational undecidability claims reported in 2026 by OpenAI and Zhi-Wei Sun imply rational-matrix undecidability, with at most $86$, $87$, and $88$ matrix variables in dimensions $1$, $2$, and at least $3$, respectively. An explicit Diophantine definition of $\mathbb Z$ in $\mathbb Q$ reported by the project coordinated by Elliot Glazer further gives completeness among computably enumerable problems. These consequences of recent arithmetic claims are stated conditionally.
item.dc:creator: Mihai Prunescu

item.title: Brauer groups of certain affine cubic surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2509.16042v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the Brauer groups of affine surfaces that are complements of singular hyperplane sections of smooth cubic surfaces over a field $k$ of characteristic $0$. We determine the Brauer group over the algebraic closure as a Galois module for all the possible singular hyperplane sections. For the case when the hyperplane section is geometrically the union of three lines, we give explicit examples where transcendental elements of order $2$ and $3$ exist over $\mathbb{Q}$. We end with an explicit example of an integral Brauer--Manin obstruction to the Hasse principle given by an element of order~$3$ on an affine cubic surface with singular boundary.
item.dc:creator: Abdulmuhsin Alfaraj

item.title: Non-equivalence of pro-$p$-Iwahori invariants
item.description: arXiv:2608.19570v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Suppose $p > 7$ is a prime number, and $F$ is a nonarchimedean local field of residual characteristic $p$ satisfying $F \neq \mathbb{Q}_p$. Generalizing results of Ghate--Le--Sheth, Le--Singh, and Huang, we show that any split, connected, reductive group $G$ over $F$ which is not a torus admits a smooth, irreducible, non-admissible mod $p$ representation. We use this to show that the functor of pro-$p$-Iwahori invariants does not induce an equivalence between the category of smooth mod $p$ $G$-representations generated by their pro-$p$-Iwahori invariant vectors and modules over the pro-$p$-Iwahori--Hecke algebra, contrary to what happens for $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_p)$.
item.dc:creator: Karol Koziol

item.title: Subset-Sum Density Realization in Locally Finite Abelian Groups
item.description: arXiv:2609.14630v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $G$ be a countable locally finite abelian group, and let \[ G_1\leq G_2\leq\cdots, \qquad \bigcup_{i\geq1}G_i=G, \] be any filtration of $G$ by finite subgroups. For $A\subseteq G$, let $\mathcal P(A)$ denote the set of all finite subset sums of elements of $A$, and let $2G:=\{2g:g\in G\}$. We prove that $|2G|=\infty$ if and only if for every filtration and every interval $[\alpha,\beta]\subseteq[0,1]$, there exists $A\subseteq G$ such that the set of limit points of \[ \left( \frac{|\mathcal P(A)\cap G_i|}{|G_i|} \right)_{i\geq1} \] is exactly $[\alpha,\beta]$. We also prove a positive-density result that does not require $|2G|=\infty$: if $G$ is infinite and $\mathcal P(A)$ has positive upper density along the given filtration, then there is an infinite set $B\subseteq \mathcal P(A)$ such that $B+B\subseteq \mathcal P(A)$. Combining this with the realization theorem, we show that, when $|2G|=\infty$, every interval $[\alpha,\beta]$ with $0\leq\alpha\leq\beta\leq1$ and $\beta>0$ can be realized by a set $A$ with this additional property.
item.dc:creator: Norbert Hegyv\'ari, Thang Pham, Boqing Xue

item.title: $2$-Large Sets and Nil-Bohr Recurrence: A Disproof of the $2$-Large Is Large Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.16605v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A set $S$ of positive integers is $r$-large if every $r$-coloring of $\mathbb{N}$ contains arbitrarily long monochromatic arithmetic progressions with common difference in $S$. We prove that every $2$-large set is a set of nil-Bohr recurrence, i.e., it meets every nil-Bohr neighborhood of $0$. This proves a conjecture of the first author and gives a sharp answer to a question of Host, Kra, and Maass. Furthermore, we show that a piecewise syndetic set is $2$-large if and only if it is nil-Bohr recurrent. From this, we show that a small modification of a set constructed by the first author is $2$-large but not $3$-large, thereby disproving the $2$-large is large conjecture of Brown, Graham, and Landman. We also deduce that the family of $2$-large sets is not partition regular, thereby answering another question of Brown, Graham, and Landman. We also show that, for every fixed nil-Bohr neighborhood $B$ of $0$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, restricting the common difference to $B$ increases the extremal number for $k$-term arithmetic progressions by at most a factor of $1+\varepsilon$, provided $k$ is sufficiently large.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Alweiss, Sohail Farhangi

item.title: The Gleason--Kahane--Zelazko theorem: a gentle introduction
item.description: arXiv:2610.39769v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: After some personal recollections of Jean-Pierre Kahane, this paper gives a gentle introduction to the Gleason-Kahane-Zelazko theorem. The theorem states that a normalised complex-linear functional on a unital complex Banach algebra is multiplicative whenever it does not vanish on invertible elements. Neither continuity of the functional nor commutativity of the algebra is assumed. We give a detailed account of three proofs: the original argument of Gleason and, independently, Kahane and Zelazko; the polynomial proof of Roitman and Sternfeld; and a proof by the author. We explain the complex analysis behind each: a special case of Hadamard's factorisation theorem, a polynomial argument using the fundamental theorem of algebra, and the Polya-Saxer theorem on zero-free entire functions and their derivatives. The elementary entire-function lemma needed for the first proof is proved in full; the Polya-Saxer theorem is used without proof. We give full details of the algebraic argument common to the three proofs, which deduces multiplicativity from the preservation of squares, including the non-commutative case. We then discuss applications and counterexamples, and present an extension to Ransford's generalised spectra using the Roitman--Sternfeld argument. We conclude with a brief guide to the more recent literature.
item.dc:creator: Catalin Badea

item.title: Infinite Generalized Sidon Sets with a Negative Answer to a Problem of Szemer\'edi
item.description: arXiv:2611.01871v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $A(x)=|A\cap[1,x]|$. For every integer $h\ge3$, every finite $B_h$ set $A_0\subseteq\mathbb N$, and every $0<c\le h^{-2/h}$, we construct an infinite $B_h$ set $A\subseteq\mathbb N$ containing $A_0$ such that $A(x)/x^{1/h}$ has upper limit $c$ and lower limit zero. This extends the range $0<c\le1/h$ obtainable from our first construction, which answered a question of Cilleruelo and Nathanson, later raised by O'Bryant, on the existence of a positive upper limit. For $h=3$, a positive upper limit disproves the assertion $A(x)=o(x^{1/3})$ in Szemer\'edi's Problem~186(d). The improved range follows from an integer lift of a modular construction of G\'omez Ruiz and Trujillo Solarte, with large gaps between sums of distinct $r$-element multisets for each fixed $1\le r<h$. These gaps ensure that successive blocks can be adjoined by translation while preserving the $B_h$ property. The same prescribed limits can be attained inside every set of asymptotic density one containing $A_0$. Separately, we construct $2^{\aleph_0}$ extensions of $A_0$ that are maximal among all $B_h$ subsets of $\mathbb N$, have the prescribed limits, and avoid any prescribed finite subset of $\mathbb N\setminus A_0$. These maximal extensions can be chosen so that $\sum_{a\in A}a^{-1/h}$ diverges arbitrarily slowly.
item.dc:creator: Guoqing Wang, Wenkai Yang

item.title: Lower intermediate dimensions of classical Denjoy minimal sets
item.description: arXiv:2611.12323v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the $\theta$-intermediate dimension of the minimal set of the classical $C^{1+\delta}$ Denjoy map, an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism of the circle not conjugate to a rigid rotation. This follows on from work of Kra and Schmeling, who showed how the box and Hausdorff dimensions may differ, depending on the Diophantine properties of the rotation number. The $\theta$-intermediate dimension interpolates between these two dimensions. We use the well-understood gap structure of the irrational rotation map to develop a covering strategy to get upper bounds on the lower $\theta$-intermediate dimension, and use results of Banaji to show that these upper bounds are sharp for $\theta$ in an interval.
item.dc:creator: Milo Edwardes
